content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: GPU pool 'dedicated-gpu-east-1' at 98% allocation, queue growth detected. Paging oncall.

pagerduty: @oncall-maya (SRE) — triggered from latency spike alert: token-latency-p90 > 1200ms for 10m, request queue > 600.

oncall-maya: I'm on it. digging into metrics now.

sre-jen: seeing sustained enqueue rate ~220 req/s, served ~70 req/s from that pool. Throttle errors spiking: 429 from runtime queue throttle.

infra-raj: constraints: dedicated-gpu-east-1 has 24 GPUs, autoscaler at max replicas 24 (quota). No new GPUs will come online without a quota bump or manual evict from other pools.

ops-luca: any recent deploys that touched batching/caching configs?

sre-jen: yes — 2 hours ago a config roll changed continuous_batching.window_ms from 8 to 80 and prefix_cache.max_entries from 2000 to 200. It was rolled in the 'batch-tuning' feature flag. suspect regression.

oncall-maya: that matches — bigger batching window + tiny prefix cache would increase request coalescing delay and reduce cache hit rate, but why queue grows? maybe longer batching holding requests -> per-GPU throughput drops.

support-sam: Customers reporting slow responses in hosted API: ticket count up 14x in last hour. Top accounts: acme-inc, travelore, studyai.

product-elena: are SLAs at risk? any affected Dedicated customers with reserved throughput?

infra-raj: Dedicated customers are impacted; autoscaler hit hard limit so no capacity. Fallback routing to other regions is enabled but not fully open for Dedicated (policy: no cross-region for reserved). Hosted (shared) still has capacity.

sre-jen: quick check — prefix cache miss ratio jumped from 12% to 68% after config change. per-GPU token throughput dropped ~45% due to batching window increase causing longer per-batch latencies.

oncall-maya: mitigation plan: (1) disable batch-tuning feature flag to revert batching/caching params, (2) temporarily route low-priority/no-SLA traffic to hosted pool (if policy allows), (3) increase autoscaler max replicas if quota allows or manually redistribute workload, (4) page infra for quota bump if needed. executing step 1 now.

oncall-maya: /feature-flag disable batch-tuning

incident-bot: feature-flag 'batch-tuning' disabled by oncall-maya.

sre-jen: rolling restart runtime pods in dedicated-gpu-east-1 to pick up reverted config. doing small batch: 3 pods at a time.

infra-raj: while restarts happen, I'll open a temporary routing rule to send 30% of non-SLA traffic to hosted-api-west as a safety valve. applying now.

ops-luca: applied routing override: non-sla -> hosted-api-west 30%.

sre-jen: logs: sample from runtime node-7 before restart:
```
[2026-03-15T14:02:10Z] request enqueue 0.012s
[2026-03-15T14:02:10Z] batching hold 0.078s (window_ms=80)
[2026-03-15T14:02:10Z] kv-cache MISS prefix_key=acct:acme-inc:conv:123
[2026-03-15T14:02:10Z] served in 2.34s
```

sre-jen: after revert, batch window shows 8ms and cache hit ratio climbing.

oncall-maya: observed queue length dropping from 1200 -> 420 within 6 minutes of first restart.

support-sam: support tickets stabilizing; customers updated: posted to status page that we're investigating and mitigation underway. Pushing brief note to affected customers (acme-inc, travelore, studyai).

product-elena: need a quick customer-impact summary for execs: estimate downtime-equivalent latency increase, affected percentage, and whether any SLA credits likely.

sre-jen: preliminary: ~65% of requests to dedicated pool experienced >2x latency; impacted customers ~0.6% of total hosts but 3 large customers saw error rate jump. Put precise numbers in postmortem.

infra-raj: autoscaler remaining at max; after revert, per-GPU throughput restored ~+50% so autoscaler no longer the bottleneck. still opening ticket with cloud account team for quota increase to avoid single-pool saturation in future.

oncall-maya: next steps: 1) finish rolling restarts (estimate 12 minutes), 2) keep routing override for 30m, 3) create incident ticket and assign postmortem to sre-jen + infra-raj + product-elena, 4) notify billing/sales for possible SLA handling.

ops-luca: rolling restarts done for first 12 pods, queue down to 180.

sre-jen: full rollout of restart complete. metrics:
- queue length peak: 1248
- queue length now: 42
- prefix cache miss: 65% -> 14%
- p90 latency per token: 1200ms -> 340ms

support-sam: status update posted at 14:25: short blurb sent to affected customers.
